Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 05/03/2026
Patient: Deanne Ortiz, 85 y/o F

Wt stable, BMI 30.0. Vitals stable, BP 130/78, HR 72. No acute distress. PE: lungs clear, heart RRR, no murmurs. Abd soft, NT, no HSM. Neuro grossly intact.

No NM dz, no NYHA III/IV CHF, no MRI need, can use remote. Labs WNL. Meds reviewed, adherence good. Discussed lifestyle mods, diet, exercise. Follow-up in 6 mo or PRN.

Plan: Continue current meds, monitor BP, labs q6mo. Encourage activity, wt control. Telehealth option available as needed.

notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 10/20/2025
Patient: Deanne Ortiz, 84 y/o F

Attended PSG 10/20/2025. Study revealed moderate-severe sleep apnea. AHI 39.1/h. CA+MA 13% of total AHI. Sleep architecture fragmented with reduced REM.

O2 sat nadir 82%, mean 93%. Periodic limb movements minimal. No significant arrhythmias noted.

Recommendations: Consider CPAP titration given severity. Follow-up in sleep clinic for management and compliance monitoring.

notes.title: Sleep Medicine Consultation
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/13/2026
Patient: Deanne Ortiz, 85 y/o F

Hx: Long-standing OSA, CPAP tx initiated 2 yrs ago.

Current Tx: CPAP 14 cmH2O, residual AHI 19.2 despite nightly use = failure.

Assessment: Persistent moderate-severe OSA despite adherence to CPAP at prescribed pressure.

Plan: Consider alternative therapies including BiPAP or advanced PAP modes. Recommend sleep study to reassess titration and evaluate for comorbid sleep disorders. Follow-up in 4 weeks to review results and adjust management accordingly.
